name: Star Ruby
spiritual: Awakens the heart and root centers
physical: Traditionally associated with vitality and stamina
Crystal healers link it to warmth and circulation of energy
Many people keep it nearby for a boost on tired days
summary: Star Ruby is a rare red corundum showing a six-rayed star on its dome, a stone of passion and courage in crystal lore, prized for devotion and vitality.
intro: Star ruby is ruby that has been cut en cabochon to reveal a six-rayed star floating on its dome. The star is an optical effect called asterism, produced by tiny rutile needles aligned inside the crystal. Because ruby only forms star patterns when rutile inclusions are abundant, the stone is rarely transparent: most star rubies are translucent, with a milky or velvety look from the inclusions. Color ranges from raspberry to deep red, and the best combine a rich hue with a sharp, complete star. They are very hard and durable, and a good one feels both ancient and vivid, a red flame with a white compass star hanging in it.
history: Ruby, known in Sanskrit as ratnaraj, the king of gems, has been prized in Asia for over two thousand years, and star stones were considered particularly potent talismans. Burmese warriors are said to have worn rubies for invulnerability in battle, and in Indian tradition the stone was offered to deities. Star rubies from Myanmar and Sri Lanka have been famed in royal collections, including the DeLong Star Ruby of over 100 carats, held by the American Museum of Natural History in New York. In the twentieth century, lab-grown star rubies appeared and made the effect widely affordable, yet fine natural ones remain scarce.
meaning: Star ruby is a stone of passion, courage and radiant devotion. The red body is linked to the heart and root centers, symbolizing life force and love, while the star adds a note of guidance and good fortune. Practitioners use it to boost confidence, to kindle motivation and to strengthen loyalty and commitment in relationships. It is also seen as a protective stone, thought to shield the wearer from discouragement and from harmful influences. People choose star ruby for moments that require courage, such as speaking up, starting a new venture or committing to a vow. Because ruby is energizing, many prefer to use it in moderation and balance it with calming stones if they feel overstimulated.
howToUse: Hold a star ruby in your hand while stating your intentions aloud, watching the star shift in the light as a sign of focus. Wear it as a ring, pendant or earring for confidence and a feeling of inner warmth. Place a cabochon on your altar for rituals of love, commitment or courage. Keep a smaller piece in a pocket during demanding days. In a grid, pair it with rose quartz and garnet for love and vitality, or with clear quartz to amplify intentions. Limit use at bedtime if you find red stones stimulating.
care: Star ruby is among the hardest of natural stones, so it can be rinsed in lukewarm water, scrubbed gently with mild soap and dried with a soft cloth. It tolerates sun, moonlight, smoke and sound for cleansing. Be mindful that many rubies are fracture-filled or heat-treated, and such stones should avoid ultrasonic and steam cleaners and harsh chemicals. Store it in a soft pouch away from other gems to prevent edge chipping, and take care with hard knocks.
identify: A natural star ruby shows six rays, often slightly wavy and set in a translucent body with silky inclusions. Synthetic star rubies, produced since the mid-twentieth century, tend to be very uniform in color with razor-sharp stars and curved growth lines under magnification. Cheap imitations are made of glass or dyed quartz, with printed stars or visible bubbles. Many natural ones are heated or filled. Because values vary hugely, a lab report is advised for any significant purchase.

faq.q: What is the difference between ruby and star ruby?
faq.a: Both are red corundum. Star ruby contains rutile needles that create a six-rayed star when cut as a dome, while regular ruby is usually faceted and transparent. Star ruby is generally translucent.

faq.q: What is star ruby good for?
faq.a: In crystal tradition, star ruby is used for courage, passion, devotion and vitality. Its star is read as a guiding light, making it a favorite for those starting something bold.

Some are natural, but many on the market are lab-created. Synthetic stars look very sharp and even with curved growth lines. Natural stones have subtler, silkier stars and cost more, so buy from trusted sellers.
